title: Recursion and stack limits
learningObjectives: Explain recursion and stack limits and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself directly or indirectly. A recursive solution needs a base case and a progress step that moves toward it. Excessive recursion can exceed the engine's call stack; iterative approaches may be more suitable for large inputs.
understand.whyItMatters: A missing or incorrect base case can cause infinite recursion. Understanding stack depth helps choose between recursion and iteration for reliable programs.
understand.analogy: Recursion is like solving a large task by solving a smaller version of the same task until a simple stopping case is reached.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: The base case stops at zero. Each call reduces n, so the function eventually reaches the base case.

examples.explanation: The base case stops at zero. Each call reduces n, so the function eventually reaches the base case.

practise.guidedTask: Write a recursive countdown and an iterative version. Test zero, negative, and large inputs and discuss stack limits.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that demonstrates the concept, test edge cases, and explain the execution or reference behaviour in your own words.

questions.explanation: A base case terminates recursion when the input reaches a stopping condition.
